lines: He is brought to the emergency department due to persistent bleeding from his umbilical stump.

The parents declined all hospital interventions after birth, including vaccinations and injections.

encounters.cc: Concern about the shape of the child's feet

lines: Concern about the shape of the child's feet

The patient is a 4-month-old male with known hereditary spherocytosis and a history of neonatal hemorrhagic disease, late-onset sepsis with meningitis, and prior hematology follow-up, who is brought to the pediatrician's office by his parents for a routine well-child visit.
The parents express concern about the shape of their child's feet, noting that the front part of the feet seems to turn inward.
They deny any history of trauma or illness.
- Vitamin K deficiency (Hemorrhagic disease of the newborn) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Normal neonatal creatinine transition (maternal creatinine transfer) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Late-onset neonatal sepsis with Group B Streptococcal meningitis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
The infant was born at term via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has met all developmental milestones appropriately.
- Father: Hereditary spherocytosis, splenectomy at age 8
- Mother: Gestational diabetes mellitus (diet controlled, resolved), Group B Streptococcus colonization during pregnancy
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
On physical examination, the infant is well-appearing and in no distress.
Inspection of the feet reveals medial deviation of the forefoot relative to the hindfoot.
Gentle lateral pressure on the forefoot results in correction of the alignment, indicating flexibility of the deformity.
There is no erythema, swelling, or tenderness, and the infant does not appear to be in pain when the feet are manipulated.
